data.name: result
data.source: app.describeConditionWrite.execute — reads the strategy fresh, composes the entire condition list with the edit applied, has BattleGrid compile it (which writes nothing), and mints the token against the text on screen

data.name: proposal
data.shape: { strategyId, consequence, conditionKey, standing, listKeys: (string|null)[], dangling: string[], plan, confirmationToken }
data.source: the 'proposal' arm of describeConditionWrite — consequence is the stored string the confirmation was issued against

data.name: existing
data.source: the strategy read fresh — the conditions as the platform sent them

data.name: parsed
data.source: draftFromQuery(searchParams) in condition-form.ts — the drafted edit, read off the query string it was tried under

data.name: problem
data.source: searchParams — the refusal a rejected saveConditions redirected back with; the rest of the query is the edit, round-tripped so a refusal returns to a describe over the same edit

components.purpose: The write half of condition authoring: show what the strategy defines, describe what saving an edit would leave it defining, and carry the one committing form.
components.current_implementation: max-w-3xl (wider than the confirm pages) centered column, space-y-6, p-6. Six of the eight post-connection branches share a `head` fragment: h1 'Save a condition to <name>' plus the problem banner when one arrived — so listing, no-such-condition, inexpressible, drift, refused and proposal each carry the banner from one rendering rather than six. `listing` (no edit, or a malformed one) explains that BattleGrid has no per-condition tool so saving anything resubmits the whole list, then shows the current list. `no-such-condition` says the named key is not defined (role=alert, rounded-gc-2 plain border, p-3) above the list. `inexpressible` renders h2 'Part of this draft cannot be sent to BattleGrid' over a role=alert list prefixed 'Not understood by Grid-Commander:', and states nothing was compiled and nothing was saved. `drift` — BattleGrid's compiled post-state does not match what was submitted — renders h2 'BattleGrid would save something other than what was submitted', lists the reasons, and states no confirmation was minted. `refused` renders h2 'BattleGrid refused this change — here is why' over the compiler's reason whole, then 'Nothing was written.' as a plain sentence. `strategy-missing` and `unreadable` are the two branches that render BEFORE `head` is built — they mirror the other strategy pages, and unreadable leads back to the strategy since without a fresh read there is nothing to compose against. Gap, recorded rather than designed around: because they precede `head`, those two branches drop a carried `?problem=` entirely. `saveConditions` catches a failed apply and redirects here with the draft plus the problem, so a bounced save whose next read then fails shows the read failure and no word of the click — the same defect `the-outcome-reaches-the-person` fixed on the six ceremony pages with the shared `CarriedProblem`, which this page does not use. One state added: `prose-names-it`, for a compile refused because the strategy's own market-read prose references the condition by marker. It names the marker and the platform's nearest key where one was given, with BattleGrid's own sentence beneath.
constraints: The whole list is the subject, never one condition — openspec/specs/strategy-authoring/spec.md:1166-1169 ('No tool writes one condition; the only path submits the whole array … A surface that spoke of writing one condition would be describing an operation the platform does not offer'). Copy and layout must keep saying what the strategy would be left defining.
The page renders whole from one server round trip — no client JS, no hydration. A design requiring client-side interactivity changes behavior and is requires-spec-change.
Each failure arm states that nothing was compiled / written / saved — 'Absence of effect is stated, not implied' (system.json principle); those sentences must keep visual commitment.

The inexpressible arm is Grid-Commander's own refusal to guess — spec.md:1172-1175 ('a composed condition carrying a form this product did not understand SHALL NOT be written back at all'); it must stay visually distinct from a platform refusal.

components.purpose: Show the refusal that bounced a submitted save back — the apply failed after the describe was agreed to.
components.current_implementation: An inline `{problem ? … : null}` block inside the shared `head` fragment, carrying DT-0004's danger treatment byte-for-byte: rounded-gc-2 border border-danger-default bg-danger-subtle p-4 text-sm text-text-primary with role=alert and a semibold 'Refused: ' prefix. It is the same paragraph the shared `CarriedProblem` component (carried-problem.tsx) now holds for the six ceremony pages, spelled out here rather than imported — this page was not in that change's scope. Because the edit round-trips in the query, the banner sits above a fresh describe of the same edit against the strategy as it now stands. It renders on six of the eight branches; `strategy-missing` and `unreadable` are built before `head` and show nothing.
constraints: role=alert must survive.
A refusal returns to the surface acted from with the edit preserved — spec.md:1177-1179; the banner and the re-described edit must stay on one page.

Whatever treatment this takes must stay identical to the shared `CarriedProblem`'s — two spellings of one paragraph is how the six ceremony pages drifted before it was extracted, and restyling only one of the two would reopen exactly that.

components.purpose: Tell the operator their draft does not describe a definition yet — a half-filled form, not a platform refusal.

actions.effect: Underlined link back to /strategies/[id]/conditions carrying the same query (minus any problem), so the draft is finished where it was composed

components.current_implementation: h2 'This draft is not finished' over a ul with role=alert (rounded-gc-2, plain border-border-default, p-3) listing the row-level problems from draftFromQuery — Grid-Commander's own wording, e.g. 'Row 2 compares spread to nothing — give it a number.' Followed by the composer link and the sentence 'nothing was compiled and nothing was saved.' Rendered inside the listing state so the list below does not read as the draft having been forgotten.
constraints: These problems are ours to say and said as ours — a malformed draft never reaches BattleGrid, so this block must not look like a platform answer.
Plain border, not danger — the fix is on the page the operator is already looking at; 'notice never borrows danger's colour' (system.json principle).
The link back to the composer must carry the draft's query — losing it turns a half-filled form into a blank one.

components.purpose: Show what the strategy defines now — the baseline every edit is an edit of.

actions.effect: Underlined link per condition to this same route with ?remove=<key> — starts a describe of the list without it

Underlined link per condition to the composer seeded from that condition (?try=1&from=<key>…), carrying its key, name and verdict so a bare click does not demote a directional call to a building block

components.current_implementation: h2 'What <name> defines now'. Empty: a text-sm text-text-secondary sentence — 'This strategy defines no conditions. Anything saved here would be its first.' Populated: a ul of rounded-gc-2 border cards, each with the condition's name, its key in text-xs uppercase with either '· a named building block' or '· calls <verdict>', the definition drawn by ConditionStructure, and the two links. This markup is inline in the page and near-duplicates ConditionCard in strategy-conditions.tsx rather than reusing it.
constraints: Empty must stay distinguishable from unreadable — spec.md:318-321 ('the strategy is shown as having no conditions … distinguished from a strategy whose conditions could not be read'); the empty sentence must not be dropped for whitespace.
A null verdict is a named building block, not an absence — spec.md:760-762 ('MUST NOT be presented as a way the strategy calls direction'); the '· a named building block' annotation must survive.
The remove and change links are behavior (they start describes) — a design may restyle them but not collapse them into one control or hide them behind interaction that needs client JS.

components.purpose: Draw one condition's definition as the structure it is — nesting shown, negation said as negation, references named.
components.current_implementation: Shared ConditionStructure component (strategy-conditions.tsx), recursive: groups render a heading ('All 3 must hold', 'Any of 2 must hold', 'Must NOT hold', '2 of 3 must hold') over an ml-4 border-l indented ul of members; comparisons read as words ('spread is below 0.5', 'regime is between 1 and 3', 'trend is “UP”'); a reference shows its key, and a reference to a key not defined here appends '— no condition with this key is defined here' in text-text-secondary; an unrecognised form renders 'Not understood by Grid-Commander: <reason>'.
constraints: Nesting is drawn, not flattened — spec.md:723-725 ('The presentation MUST show that nesting rather than flatten it'); a member of a NOT means the opposite of the same member outside it.
NOT is said as negation, never as a count — '0 of 1 must hold' reads as a mistake (the component's own ruling).
A dangling reference is never silently omitted — the reader must not see a shorter condition than the one that exists.
Shared with every surface that draws a condition — restyle it once, in the component, or the two renderings of the grammar will disagree about a negation eventually.

components.purpose: State what agreeing does — the edit, the whole list, and how many agents are reconfigured — in the exact text the confirmation was issued against.
components.current_implementation: whitespace-pre-line rounded-gc-2 border border-border-default p-4 text-sm with role=alert — the stored multi-line consequence string, rendered verbatim. Plain border, not the consequence-subtle treatment DT-0004 gave the agent ceremonies.
constraints: The text is the string the token was minted against — never a second wording of it; a design must not paraphrase, truncate, or summarize (spec.md:1222-1226: the list, whether the edit added/replaced/removed, what it strands, and the bound-agent count are 'part of the text the confirmation is issued against').
The bound-agent count is stated whether zero or many — spec.md:1241-1243 ('never omitted'); 'Unknown is not zero' (system.json principle).
whitespace-pre-line must survive — the stored string carries its own line structure.
Consequence outranks everything on a screen (system.json principle).
role=alert must survive.

components.purpose: Name every condition the strategy would be left defining, because the platform takes the list whole.
components.current_implementation: h2 'The whole list that would be submitted', a text-text-secondary sentence stating every entry is resubmitted and the resulting count, then an ordered list of keys — the edited key annotated with '— <standing>' (added / replaced / removed phrasing from the describe). A key-less entry renders as '(an entry with no key)'. Empty: 'None — the strategy would define no conditions at all.'
constraints: The list is stated, not just the edit — spec.md:1245-1249 ('all three are named as what the strategy would be left defining … the text says the platform takes the condition list whole').
The empty case is a real, submittable outcome (removing the last condition) and must keep its own sentence — silence reads as a broken page.
The standing annotation tells the operator whether their draft joined or replaced — spec.md:1188-1192; it must stay attached to the key it describes.

components.purpose: Name every reference the edit would leave with nothing to resolve — shown, not blocked.
components.current_implementation: h2 'These references would have nothing to resolve', a ul with role=alert (plain border-border-default) — '<key> is referred to by a condition in the list above and defined by none of them' — and a text-text-secondary coda: 'Shown, not blocked. Whether BattleGrid accepts a dangling reference is its ruling to make, and it will say so in its own words.'
constraints: Shown and never blocking — spec.md:1238-1239 ('A dangling reference SHALL be shown and SHALL NOT block the write'); a design must not style this as an error that implies the submit is disabled.
Only references the EDIT strands appear here — pre-existing dangling references are the strategy's own and are reported where it is read (spec.md:1234-1236); a design must not merge the two.
role=alert must survive.

components.purpose: Carry the agreement: apply exactly the plan that was reviewed, and no other.

actions.effect: POSTs the server action with strategyId, the compiled plan as JSON, the confirmationToken, and the draft query; success lands on the strategy read fresh, any failure redirects back here with the edit preserved and ?problem=

components.current_implementation: flex flex-wrap gap-3; four hidden inputs (strategyId, plan JSON, confirmationToken, draft). The plan travels through the form because what is applied must be what was reviewed — it is not trusted; the confirmation is bound to strategy:<id>#<intentDigest>, so a plan altered in transit digests differently and the write is refused before BattleGrid is asked.
constraints: The hidden binding is the ceremony — the form must keep exactly one submit path, and the plan/token pairing must not be redesigned into separate steps (spec.md:1210-1213: a confirmation cannot be spent on a different plan).
Cancel must remain a visible peer of the submit, never a text link beneath it (DT-0002 ruling, restated in control.ts).

components.purpose: Commit the write. Labelled 'Save this condition list' — the list, because the list is what is written.
components.current_implementation: BUTTON_PRIMARY constant from control.ts — accent.default bg, min-h-control (44px), rounded-gc-2, DT-0004 hover/active. No pending/loading state between click and redirect — same class of gap as #153; behavior, not styling. DT-0022 added the primitive's `disabled` treatment to this constant — bg.sunken ground, text.disabled label, border.subtle edge and cursor not-allowed, stated rather than an opacity. Defined and available; **nothing in the product enters it**, because entering `disabled` removes an affordance and is #153's question for /propose rather than a styling decision.
constraints: The label names the list, not the single condition — renaming it to 'Save this condition' would misdescribe the operation (spec.md:1166-1169).
Styling changes go through the BUTTON_PRIMARY constant in control.ts.
44px minimum tap target (system.json principle).
Focus ring comes from the one global rule in globals.css — do not add a per-element ring.

components.purpose: Decline the change and return to the strategy, leaving everything as it is.
components.current_implementation: An anchor wearing BUTTON_SECONDARY — inline-flex centering, min-h-control, DT-0004 hover. Label 'Leave things as they are'. Beneath the form, every state also carries plain underlined links 'Back to <name>' and 'Compose a condition'.
constraints: Must remain an anchor (pure navigation, no form participation) and must remain a visible peer of the submit.
Styling changes go through the BUTTON_SECONDARY constant in control.ts.
44px minimum tap target (system.json principle).

components.purpose: Reassure someone staring at a failed read that the strategy still exists, by naming the accurate external cause.
components.current_implementation: Shared WhyNotLoaded component (why-not-loaded.tsx), rendered only in the unreadable state; the way back is the strategy, because without a fresh read there is nothing to compose an edit against.
constraints: The two causes must stay distinguishable — a 401 is not an outage.
The reassurance sentence is the point and must not be cut for space.

components.purpose: Turn away a request without authority, with the one remedy that works: connect.
components.current_implementation: Shared NotConnected component (require-connection.tsx): h1 + message, connect link as an anchor wearing BUTTON_SECONDARY (DT-0006). Inherited by every authenticated page.
constraints: Every no-authority cause renders this same page by design (see design W-C) — a design must not invent per-cause variants.

flows.name: Save a drafted condition
steps: arrive from the composer with the draft in the query
the describe compiles the whole list with the draft applied
read the consequence, the resulting list, and anything stranded
land on the strategy read fresh, showing the list as the platform now holds it

flows.name: Remove a condition
steps: click 'Remove it from the strategy' on the list
the describe compiles the list without it, naming any reference left dangling
submit, or leave things as they are

flows.name: The draft is not finished
steps: 'This draft is not finished' lists the rows' problems in our words
follow 'Finish it in the composer' with the draft intact

flows.name: BattleGrid refuses the compile
steps: the describe runs and the compiler declines
the platform's reason, whole, with 'Nothing was written.'

flows.name: The apply is refused after agreement
steps: the apply fails (revision moved, token expired, platform declined)
redirected back with the edit preserved and ?problem=
a fresh describe of the same edit under the refusal banner

accessibility.notes: The problem banner, consequence, malformed/inexpressible/drift/dangling lists and the refused reason carry role=alert — so most branches announce two alerts when a reason rides in, the carried one first. `strategy-missing` and `unreadable` render before the shared head and announce no carried reason at all. Focus ring is global (focus-visible, 2px). No client JS: every state change is a full navigation; the draft travels as a query string an operator can keep, share, or edit by hand.
